items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: managed to pick a few gigs with Kaiser Marshall... I did quite a few gigs with Kaiser

ctx.x: Then I started hanging around the Rhythmn Club again and managed to pick a few gigs with Kaiser Marshall, the first well known drummer of the Fletcher Henderson orchestra. And there was a little fellow who played alto sax not very well who was named Leon Gross, but all the musicians called him Bossman, who got quite a few gigs also. Times were difficult as the Depression was still on in the USA, and musicians accepted jobs for whatever price they could get.

Kaiser called a dollar a potato and when he would ask me if I would do a gig with him, he would explain that the job only paid three potatoes. And there was a saying amongst musicians that if you did not want the gig, there was a boy around the corner that would accept it. And I was one of the boys around the corner....I did quite a few

gigs with Kaiser and Bossman. The bands were usually good musicians and there were never any hard arrangements to be played because there were always different musicians for each gig except for two or three regular musicians that Kaiser and Bossman could depend on being free at any time to accept a gig from them.
